name: r5-m02
statement: Within a problem, the cued base's finished wrong samples are premature commitments (shorter than their right siblings) on MATH Levels 1-3 and wandering attempts (longer than their right siblings) on Level 5, while RL has removed the short premature stops, so RL's finished wrong samples are longer than their right siblings at every level; hence a shortest-sample rule helps the base only where its errors are long (hard, tied problems) and gains RL nothing because RL's few ties carry little room.
scope: Covers Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token opening cue and Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (plain), MATH-500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, finished samples only (cap hits excluded), comparisons within a problem among its 4 Day-1 #3 samples (attempt 0). Does not cover T 0.6 cells (where loops dominate long failures), the harder 328 (almost all Level-5-like, no level labels), across-problem length effects (which follow difficulty), Code, or the weight-blend/Think-SFT models. Conflicts checked: result-cbe0bc's RL tie-break null is listed below.

imports.finding: Within one question the shortest sampled chain is more often right than a random or the longest chain (LN-Super 63.4 vs 47.7 vs 28.9), measured on AIME/HMMT-level problems with reasoning models; capped samples excluded.
imports.how: Taken as the hard-problem / RL-like regime: it holds for the base only on Level 5, where wrong samples wander, and for RL at every level; on easy problems the base reverses it because its wrong samples stop early.

explains.quote: breaking vote ties by the shortest finished sample gives base+cue 453/500
explains.how: Vote ties occur on hard problems where the base's wrong samples are long wandering attempts, so the shortest finished sample is more often right there.
RL no longer stops early with a wrong answer, so its short answers are essentially never wrong.
The base makes very short premature stops that RL does not, the short-wrong failure mode the theory assigns to the base on easy problems.

explains.quote: Base items with a right sibling: 39 of 48 slip/misread/format
explains.how: On problems the base can solve, its wrong samples are slips, misreads and format failures of a quick commitment, not wrong plans that wander.
Level 5 is where the base's errors switch to long wandering attempts, the regime RL improves most.

conflicts.how: If RL's wrong samples are longer at every level the shortest tie-break should help RL too; the theory has to attribute the null to RL's few ties (474-476 of 500) rather than to length carrying no signal for RL.

rival: Slips accumulate with length (r3-surprises-1): every extra step is another chance to err, so wrong finished samples are longer than right siblings at every difficulty and the base's tie-break gain is just the hard-problem share of ties. Separating observation: on Levels 1-3 the rival gives a positive within-problem log length ratio (wrong longer) and a below-chance share of wrong samples that are the shortest; this theory gives a negative ratio and an above-chance share there, with the sign flipping to positive on Level 5.

predictions.experiment: Base+cue, Levels 1-3: median over problems of the within-problem log length ratio of finished-wrong samples to their right siblings.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json (key problems; fields index, level, base_k). Keep rows with attempt == 0 (samples 0-3). Keep problems in pool_k_le3 with base_k in {1,2,3} and level in {1,2,3}. Per row: right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap-hit rows are dropped entirely (neither right nor wrong). For each kept problem with at least one finished-wrong row and at least one right row: m = median n_new of its right rows; for each finished-wrong row r_i = ln(n_new_i / m); problem value = mean of its r_i. Problems lacking a right or a finished-wrong attempt-0 row, or missing from rows.jsonl, are excluded. Statistic = median of the problem values (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values).

predictions.experiment: Base+cue, Level 5: the same within-problem log length ratio.
predictions.recipe: Same files, filters and computation as the Levels 1-3 statistic (attempt == 0; base_k in {1,2,3} from pool_k_le3.json; right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap hits dropped; per problem the mean over its finished-wrong rows of ln(n_new / median n_new of its right rows); problems lacking either kind excluded), but keep only problems with level == 5. Statistic = median of the problem values.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test, base+cue Levels 1-3: the share of finished-wrong samples shorter than every right sibling. The nearest rival (slips accumulate with length, r3-surprises-1) puts wrong samples on the long side, giving about 0.2 or less (below the ~0.3 a length-blind null gives for 1-3 right siblings); premature commitment gives well above chance.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json. Keep rows with attempt == 0; problems with base_k in {1,2,3} and level in {1,2,3}. Right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap-hit rows dropped. Over all finished-wrong rows (pooled across problems) whose problem has at least one right attempt-0 row: count a row as a hit if its n_new is strictly less than the n_new of every right row of the same problem (a tie with any right row is not a hit). Statistic = hits / number of such finished-wrong rows.

predictions.experiment: RL plain, all levels: the within-problem log length ratio of finished-wrong to right siblings.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json (fields index, level, rl_k). Keep rows with attempt == 0; keep problems in pool_k_le3 with rl_k in {1,2,3}, any level. Right = score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = cap_hit false and score_v3 == 0; cap-hit rows dropped. For each problem with at least one finished-wrong and one right row: problem value = mean over its finished-wrong rows of ln(n_new / median n_new of its right rows). Problems lacking either kind excluded. Statistic = median of problem values.

predictions.experiment: GPU: base Olmo-3-1025-7B with the cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, 8 new samples per problem (seed base 90,000,000 + index + 10,000*sample, no restarts) on the MATH-500 problems of pool_k_le3.json with level in {1,2,3}, graded with grader v3 via jobs/run_cell.py on one H100. Per problem with at least one right and one finished-wrong sample (cap hits dropped), compute for each finished-wrong sample whether its n_new is below the median n_new of the problem's right samples; report the pooled fraction.
